name: bupivacaine
notes: Long-acting amide LA; the most CARDIOTOXIC of the common amides (fast-in/slow-out avid cardiac Na-channel binding) — the stereochemistry/cardiotoxicity differentiation is v0.6 LA2. Highly bound (~95%) with SATURABLE binding, so free fraction rises non-linearly at high total concentration (the under-prediction-when-risk-is-highest failure mode, surfaced in v0.6 LA3). Concentrations in ug/mL.

protein_binding.note: ~95% bound, principally to α1-acid glycoprotein; binding SATURATES, so the free (toxic) fraction rises non-linearly when total concentration is highest. This LA-specific saturation failure mode is surfaced in v0.6 LA3; it is distinct from the v0.5 albumin/hypoalbuminemia axis (binding_sensitive=false).

free_fraction_model.note: Representative capacity-limited (Langmuir, 1:1) saturable binding to α1-acid glycoprotein. Capacity ≈ AAG molar concentration (~0.7 g/L ÷ ~41 kDa ≈ 17 µM, 1 high-affinity site) × bupivacaine MW (288 g/mol) ≈ 4.9 µg/mL drug-equivalent; the affinity is pinned by the curated low-concentration fraction_bound (0.95). Tier-D: the QUALITATIVE rise of the free fraction toward 1 as total approaches the binding capacity is well-documented (Tucker & Mather 1979 concentration-dependent binding); the magnitude is illustrative, NOT a fitted model — it makes the documented under-prediction of free-drug risk visible, never a precise prediction (v0.6 LA3, §7).

cardiotoxicity_class.mechanism: Racemic; avid 'fast-in/slow-out' use-dependent cardiac Na-channel binding plus high lipophilicity — the most cardiotoxic common amide. Cardiovascular collapse can occur with little or no CNS prodrome, so the CNS warning margin is narrow or absent.
cardiotoxicity_class.note: The reference point against which the S-enantiomers (levobupivacaine, ropivacaine) were developed. Agent-choice differentiation surfaced in v0.6 LA2; the narrow margin is why the cardiovascular threshold matters even at a similar CNS threshold.
